Team — forwarding Acme's request. TL;DR: they want two 90m blocks same day (EMEA/US) plus a 30m load test attached to the US slot. Can we avoid duplicating the entire workshop? Options:

1) Single run with mirrored cohort: run core walkthrough once, split breakout exercises across regions, run a synchronous 30m load test during US session where EMEA watches the summary. Pros: less prep. Cons: EMEA loses hands-on time.

2) Two separate 90m runs with slightly different hands-on prompts; the second run uses cached model state and a warmed routing policy so cost is lower. Pros: both regions get hands-on time. Cons: extra ops coordination and may need dedicated capacity for the load window.

Technical asks I need answered from infra:
- Can hosted pathway sustain a 30m 100-concurrent connection short burst without SLA risk? (Ben)
- If we need a Dedicated bump for the load test, what lead time and cost? (Rishi)
- If we mirror content, what's the minimal set of prompt variants to cover both cohorts? (Aditya)

I attached the draft runbook and prompt inventory template — fill the red sections and reply-all with feasibility and preferred option by EOD so I can confirm with Acme.

Evelyn

Evelyn — quick check from an ops perspective: hosted can handle a simulated load test if we keep the test to token-level replay and avoid sustained sampling spikes. For a 30-minute 100-concurrent simulated client burst, we should be fine with throttles in place, but we need two things: a) a pre-warm window of 15 minutes to populate KV caches and b) a fallback plan if latency crosses our SLO (automatic fallback to smaller model variant).

Estimate: cost delta minimal if we keep it in hosted and use the warmup + short burst pattern. If Acme insists on real streaming clients all hitting at once with long generations, we'd recommend a Dedicated temporary bump (Rishi — can you add the cost estimate?).

Also — we should change the EMEA slot slightly to 14:30–16:00 BST (shifts their start 30m later) so we can run the core walkthrough at 11:00 ET and the US hands-on at 11:30 ET with overlap for the load test at 12:00 ET. That preserves a compact schedule and avoids duplicate walkthroughs. If we do that, we can run the same slides and switch prompts in the second half.

Ben
